result.finding: Assessed 5 CWE rules in Credentials & Secrets: 1 FOUND, 4 NOT_FOUND
evidence: Reviewed SecurityConfig, application profiles, docker-compose, Dockerfile, Oracle initialization scripts, .env.example and tracked documentation. Production database/admin passwords are required environment inputs; BCrypt is used for the in-memory admin hash. Fixed usernames are identifiers, not secret credentials. Example placeholders and explicitly test-only H2/admin settings are not treated as deployed secrets. No embedded production password, immutable cryptographic key, private key or verified API token was identified in reviewed text. Gallery reads are explicitly public by design, mutation routes require authentication, and Oracle grants are schema-scoped; no confirmed permission-assignment defect under these five rules was established. Git history, actual environment values, container image contents and deployed permissions were not scanned. All secret-like values are withheld from assessment evidence.
NOT_FOUND does not certify that the repository/history or deployment contains no secrets.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Password
values.assessment_scope: repository source and tracked config, not history/runtime
values.description: The product contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for its own inbound authentication or for outbound communication to external components.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
values.assessment_scope: repository source and tracked config, not history/runtime
values.description: The product uses a hard-coded, unchangeable cryptographic key.

values.name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource
values.assessment_scope: repository source and tracked config, not history/runtime
values.description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.

values.name: Insufficient Logging

evidence.explanation: PhotoServiceImpl.deletePhoto logs the deleted photo ID and DetailController repeats the ID/success result, but neither records the authenticated principal or a request/correlation identifier. Upload success/rejection logs likewise omit the actor. SecurityConfig enables HTTP Basic without an application security-audit listener or explicit authentication-event logging. The confirmed gap is missing actor attribution for destructive operations, not complete absence of logging. Upstream proxy/SIEM/runtime audit controls were not available for inspection.

values.assessment_scope: repository source and tracked config, not history/runtime
values.description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
values.assessment_scope: repository source and tracked config, not history/runtime
values.description: The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key.
